name: Comment from Anonymous
text:
I am writing to express my concerns about the improper practices by several franchisors in the hospitality industry, specifically Choice Hotel Inc., Wyndham Hotels and Resorts, and Best Western International. As a franchisee, I have experienced firsthand the undue burden of unnecessary and escalating fees imposed by these franchisors.

These brands continuously add fees under various pretexts, such as technology fees, without delivering any tangible improvements to the technology. Despite paying these fees, we frequently encounter system crashes and slowdowns, sometimes multiple times a week, which severely handicap our operations.

Moreover, these franchisors are constantly looking for ways to introduce new penalties for franchisees, further increasing the financial strain on us. While franchisors are quick to penalize franchisees for any customer dissatisfaction, it is important to remember that we, the franchisees, are also customers to the franchisors. We are often left with no recourse, stuck in binding contracts, and hampered by subpar technology and unfair penalty fees.

Additionally, the mandatory Group Purchasing Organizations (GPOs) set by these franchisors often have higher prices than what we can obtain on our own. We are required to buy from certain approved vendors who charge more, likely because the brands receive kickbacks from these vendors. While we understand the need for uniformity across the brand, this practice unfairly increases our operational costs.

Hotel franchises also face disproportionately high Online Travel Agency (OTA) fees compared to other industries. For example, the airline industry faces OTA fees of around 3-4%, whereas the hotel industry deals with fees as high as 15%. This disparity adds another layer of financial pressure on hotel franchises.

Furthermore, franchisors impose mandatory reward programs, forcing us to enroll a specific number of customers each month. If we fail to meet the quota, we are penalized. We are required to give 5% of our room revenue to the franchisors for these rewards, yet there is no transparency on what happens to the funds not used for rewards. This system appears to be another way for franchisors to generate revenue while focusing excessively on enrolling customers.

Most of us hoteliers are small business owners who join franchises seeking industry guidance, but we often end up feeling exploited.

It is crucial for the FTC to recognize and address these unfair practices. Franchisees need better protections against these exploitative fees and more reliable technology support from franchisors.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

name: Comment from Anonymous
text:
This is a formal comment on Golden Krust Franchising, Inc. (“Golden Krust”) for multiple blatant violations of the Franchise Rule, as evidenced by their Franchise Disclosure Documents (FDDs) from 2005 to 2023, supporting documentation, and factual evidence uncovered in litigation. Violations uncovered in litigation should automatically trigger FTC investigation, in my opinion, just like they would trigger an SEC investigation regarding financial fraud- as this is no different. These violations have misled potential franchisees and harmed the overall integrity of the franchise system.

Price Discrimination: Evidence from the Auctus Restaurant Group case shows clear evidence of price discrimination between family-owned franchises and non-family-owned franchises. This discriminatory pricing practice is a violation of the FTC Act's prohibition against unfair or deceptive acts or practices in commerce.

Unfair or Deceptive Practices: Evidence suggests that Golden Krust engaged in unfair or deceptive practices by charging inconsistent royalty and advertising fees, favoring family-owned franchises with lower fees than non-family-owned franchises. This discriminatory pricing practice is a violation of the FTC Act's prohibition against unfair or deceptive acts or practices in commerce.

Misleading Financial Performance Representations (FPRs): Golden Krust's FDDs consistently lack transparency regarding the financial performance of their company-owned stores. The provided information is insufficient for potential franchisees to make informed decisions about the profitability and viability of the business model. This is particularly concerning given the evidence of preferential treatment for family-owned franchises, which could significantly skew the overall FPR data. This lack of transparency raises serious questions about Golden Krust's compliance with the Franchise Rule's requirement for a reasonable basis and substantiation for FPRs.

Inadequate Disclosure of Parent Company Financials: Golden Krust's FDDs fail to consistently and clearly identify Golden Krust Bakery as the parent company, despite its significant control over franchise operations, including supply and distribution. This lack of disclosure misrepresents the financial health and stability of the overall business structure, potentially misleading potential franchisees. The Franchise Rule mandates the disclosure of parent company financials when the parent guarantees the franchisor's obligations, which is the case with Golden Krust Bakery's extensive control over the franchise system.
Omission of Material Litigation: Golden Krust's FDDs do not consistently disclose all material litigation, particularly disputes with franchisees over fees and product pricing. This omission deprives potential franchisees of crucial information needed to assess the risks associated with the franchise investment. The Franchise Rule requires the disclosure of litigation that could materially impact the franchise system, and Golden Krust's selective disclosure raises concerns about their compliance. After Golden Krust lost litigation over price, royalty, and advertising discrimination in 2020 they failed to produce FDD’s for 2 years, concealing the litigation to current and potential franchisees, further, in violation to the Franchise Rule, continued to market and sell franchise locations during this period.

Failure to Update FDD After Material Change: Golden Krust failed to update its FDD for nearly two years after a 2020 ruling in the Auctus Restaurant Group case, which found their pricing practices unfair and discriminatory. This delay in disclosing a material change in the franchise system could be a violation of the Franchise Rule.

Given the gravity of these potential violations, I urge the FTC to thoroughly investigate Golden Krust Franchising, Inc.'s practices and take appropriate enforcement action to protect the interests of franchisees and maintain the integrity of the franchise industry.

name: Comment from HOW2 B Solar LLC
text:
I bought 2 Franchises from Solar Grids in 2021 as an investment. I had 3 calls with different representatives, a zoom call with some franchisees at the moment. I asked more than once about the initial investment amount and at least in 2 occasions (always over the phone) the CEO of the company said and I quote "almost nothing". Solar Grids was offering lead generation, multiples ways of income, commercial deals. I was offered a lead generation program (100 leads in 3 months) for $ 5500.- per month. This program did not provide any leads. The owner of the marketing company suggested by Solar Grids suddenly appeared as owning a solar franchise. I cut one of my consultancy contracts at the time to a part time (losing $ 3500.- a month for many months) to dedicate time to the business. When I got my sales team, the struggles started: 1.Solar Grids did not provide the help or support services we needed. They never had a program to produce leads which are part of their franchise opportunity offer (please, refer to their website). The multiple versions of sales training that the General Manager and the sales Reps had, had no structure or worth, even after many of us (both franchisees and sales reps) asked for specific areas of help. Our questions went unanswered and critical problems were not addressed and often ignored. 2.The solar sales software/app we were to use (Quativa) did not supply adequate products, and support needed to be successful selling solar energy systems. Quativa was selected by Solar Grids to manage our solar sales, but our sales proposals would constantly expire unexpectedly and oftentimes, overnight with no warning. Communication was nonexistent. Solar Grids had only one tech person who would act as intermediary between Quativa and us. Needless to say that this person could not handle all the different requests and issues for all the franchisees. 3.The only installation company provided to install our solar projects in FL was inadequate in both communication and following appropriate procedures for installing solar energy systems on residential roofs. Our customers were often frustrated and confused and our ability to find solutions was ignored. One of the 3 clients we had, had the installation without the proper permits and ended up paying for the solar loan and the utility bill for months. Solar Grids failed to remediate neither attempted to remediate the situation. This type of issues happened in Florida with many clients, even from other franchisees in the state.
4.To solve these third parties installations issues (Solar Grids said they would handle the installation when I bought the territories) they started offering an installation franchise so each franchisee would be able to control the whole process. Despite offering to waive the initial fee, they had a $ 15000.- training fee and tons of other monthly costs for support. The business model had changed.
5.By October 2022, I had consumed all the money I had in renting the office, fees for the general manager, travel expenses, marketing expenses, fees for a social media manager, ipads, phones, & others. At that moment it was clear that Solar Grids had been advertising a totally different business model than what I had bought. 6.Solar Grids offered a turnkey opportunity, and failed to give us the support and the leads, failed in being truthful about the real investment, suddenly stop allowing commercial sales (we learned this around May 2022) and changed the rules and the business model on the go. This is not what I bought.

Most of these vendors are incompetent, uncaring of franchisee needs, and poorly capitalized.  They demand deposits and prepayments from hotel owners as if they don’t have the ability to produce or deliver goods without collecting our money upfront.  IHG employees always harassing owners to give business to these so called vendors.

name: Comment from Anonymous
text:
I am writing this anonymously for fear of retaliation. We purchased Dickey's Barbecue Pit Franchise in 2018. Prior to the purchase, we were provided false information regarding the buildout cost and revenue stream. We realized we were intentionally misguided when we were half way into the project. By then, it was too late to back out.

During the buildout, we were forced to purchase furniture from Standford Sonoma, a stored owed by Dickey's Corporation, at exorbitant prices - about three times the cost of the furniture in other stores. We were also forced to purchase equipment from Central Restaurants which offers kickbacks to Dickey's Corporation. We were also forced to purchase signage and other accessories from designated stores owned and operated by Dickey's Corporation. In fact, the entire scheme of opening a Dickey's restaurant was fraudulently designed to enrich Dickey's Corporation. We are shocked that Dickey's Corporation has managed to defraud people into opening Restaurants only for the restaurant to go out of business the first or second year.
People's life savings have been wiped out by this fraudulent act and Dickey's Corporate should be investigated. Their stores are closing more than any restaurant chain in the United States for this reason.

Owner Operators are also forced to buy food products from USFoods exclusively from a list the Corporate provided to the vendor. It costs three times more to purchase the food items from USFoods than other stores. The exhorbitant prices were designed to benefit Dickey's Corporation.

When we signed the Franchise Agreement, 50% of the marketing fees we pay weekly was supposed to be utilized to support Owner Operator marketing needs. Dickey's Corporation violated this contractual clause by reneging on their commitment to return 50% of the marketing fees to Owner Operators for local marketing. In addition to the 5% royalty, Dickey's Corporation also keeps the entire 4% marketing fee each Owner Operator pays for marketing. This is theft!

The aggressive discounts and many promotions run continuously month after month hurt profitability and violates the Franchise Agreement we signed. Promotions were only meant to be for a limited time, not indefinitely. Dickey's Corporate provides no mechanism or transparency for Owner Operators to track and ensure that they are being reimbursed for these endless promotions. Also, Dickey's Corporation
tends to extend the deep discounts to our third party vendors (Ubereats, Doordash, Grubhub, etc.) without the consent or knowledge of Owner Operators. These tactics are all designed to generate marginal revenue for the Corporation at the expense and deep losses of Owner Operators.

Furthermore, the SPARKS technology weekly and monthly fees that are deducted from our accounts were not disclosed in the Franchise Agreement. These payments are illegal and Dickey's Corporation continue to deduct these fees from our accounts. Furthermore, the Corporation offers no protection for fraudulent purchases made in SPARKS.
They push the burden to Owner Operators who are also forced to maintain the system. Dickey’s continue to make contractual changes via the Operations Manual which is immoral and unethical at the expense of Owner Operators.

Once you open your store, you do not get any type of help from Dickey's Corporation. First, they rip you off from all the furniture, equipment, signage and other accessories they force you to purchase from designated stores. Second, they continue to rip you off from their food vendor and deep discounts and promotions they run endlessly, including extending those discounts to the third party vendors without the knowledge or consent of Owner Operators. Third, they deduct whatever amount they feel like deducting from your account without any form of transparency or accountability. Fourthly, they provide you with no help at all. This Corporation has ruined a lot of lives and must be investigated. They are fraudulent. Please come to the rescue of many investors that have lost everything they worked hard for their entire lives. This fraud must stop and it must stop now. Please launch an investigation by contacting Owner Operators of every Dickey's Barbecue Pit store that are open and closed to validate every statement I have made in this complaint. Dickey's Corporation cannot be allowed to continue to ruin lives with their deceitful and fraudulent business model. Thank you!

name: Comment from Anonymous
text:
My comments are regarding the constant changes and violations of our Franchise Agreements. I have stated the "Promotions" violation to Dickey's Barbecue Restaurant International (DBRI). They do not respond to my communication and continue the behavior.
1.The Coke & Brand Champion Rebates- We cannot receive them without completing the ever changing rules & documentation requirements. Yet we are the purchaser of the Coke products. 2.The Operating Manual (OM) available online is from 2016, we are told that we are out of compliance but the current OM states differently. 3. Brand Standards is a word thrown around constantly, but there is not actually a list of Brand Standards. "Brand Standards" is used against the owner who argues with any subject. 4.When we opened our restaurant, we managed our menu, we could make items available or not, as needed. DBRI took this away last year. They stated owners were abusing the option. Now we must request a Regional Business Leader to access the menu and make changes. Sometimes they don't respond or have gone to bed for the night, & we are stuck with customer calls & complaints. 5. When DBRI runs a Limited Time Only (LTO), they "autoship" the initial items, then we order more if we need it. When the LTO is over, US Foods is instructed to autoship the balance of the items. These items have already been removed from all sites (POS, OLO, 3PV) to sell. We are stuck with the items at full price and must discard once expired. This is a financial hardship on the already struggling restaurant. 6. DBRI has created their own supply warehouse, called Wycliff Douglas. Many items come from this warehouse through our current ordering system, US Foods. Many items come to us as a "Direct Ship" with additional shipping costs, these items arrive by UPS, USPS or FedEx. All of the Dry Goods have moved to Direct Ship, causing additional Cost of Goods (COGs). Our COGs are getting too high to continue ordering this way. 7. DBRI owns a company associated with creating and supplying Dickey's restaurant locations. Stanford Sonoma is owned by DBRI, not disclosed. They supplied our interior items, such as tables, chairs, & wood siding, at an increased costs of other same business types. They required us to purchase the potato slicer from Stanford Sonoma. This was $300.00 more than the cost at WebStraunt for the exact same item. They use the Big Yellow Cup email & phone number systems, to sell their own products directly out of the Home Office "Barbecue At Home, By Dickey's" Using the website athome.dickeys.com. This directly competes with our restaurants and our ability to sell our meats, they attached these advertisements while discounting our menu. They sold pellets, barbecue sauce, & meats. 8. I have asked numerous times what my Marketing Fees are being used for. DBRI doesn't have National Marketing, this we have requested. The FA states local marketing is the responsibility of the Owners. Until recently the pictures and materials listed on Facebook and Instagram were old/recycled photos and statements/discounts. Several new owners have stated the marketing fund is called the "slush fund". 9. My Franchise Agreement states occasional Promotions, we run on an average 10 promos daily. Customers are emailed and text free or deep discounted offers, that the Owners are not aware of. Discounts that We have Opted out of on 3PV, will still appear or other offers that We were not notified of. We must check our Dashboards daily to see what is being offered. 9. DBRI refuses to negotiate our 3PV contracts, we are currently at 27% fees to DoorDash & UberEats. 10. The Owners ability to manage our menus has now moved to include Pricing. We cannot increase our prices, especially for the 3PV. 3PV continue to collect 27% fees and DBRI collects 9% & We can't change anything. 11. I have expressed to DBRI the cost of doing business in California vs Texas, without response. In California minimum wage is double that of Texas, insurance and rents are greater too. Even our US Food pricing is higher than in Texas. They do not take in consideration the cost of doing business, in the various Regions across the US. 12. We constantly have IT issues, promos that shouldn't continue or don't include all the required food items. Many times the website doesn't work correctly, causing multiple orders and order disputes with the credit card companies. These are at the cost of the Owners, We are not reimbursed for the mistakes.
